question: Can a learned affine bridge convey a supplied verified mathematical proof to a general model more usefully than the exact same proof supplied as text?
scope: Proof-assisted one-token choice in constructive implication graphs. An engineering and exploratory reasoning experiment, not equal-information pretraining skill transfer.

pilot.purpose: Pipeline checks only; no capability conclusion from these30prompts.

expanded.train_grammar: parallel disjoint routes, varying path lengths
expanded.val_grammar: three disjoint routes, varying path lengths
test_grammars: two chained diamonds with a directed cycle
expanded.structural_grouping: All renamings of the same rooted route-length/cycle/distractor signature stay within one split. Full topology grammars held out; only2testgrammars, so family-level uncertainty is weak.

interface.boundary: hidden_states[14], after decoder layer13 for a28-layer Qwen2 model; verify installed implementation before hooking
interface.device: MPS after a3-example CPU float32 smoke run
interface.input_format: literal text, no chat template, no special tokens

fit.selection: Lowest validation normalized RMSE, ties smalleralpha. Fixedlayer14, no test-based choice. Train-only scaling and no valrefit.

functional.label_check: Require exactly one continuation token per label and stable promptprefix tokenization.
controls: recipient with identical donor proof text
oracle recipient state from text-assisted prompt
functional.selection: Fixed test set, no intervention mixing/layer tuning on test.

budget.model_loading: Sequential, one checkpoint per process; local24GiBAppleM5Pro.
budget.student: Fixed small student versus equal token/step budget control, after functional experiment. No iterative generation before measurable fixed-data value.

limitations: The source receives a verified certificate; this is explicit assistance, not knowledge acquired by the recipient.
Choice candidates have equal length, one invalid; all original goals are reachable.
Expanded data still synthetic and restricted; report failures and weak family-level power.
